OCT 15th - 🚀 Vilnius Founders: Building Global Brands with Marius Buzaitis, Co-Founder of Orbio World!

Orbio World (https://orbio.world/) is a rapidly growing Lithuanian e-commerce and product development company that builds consumer brands and sells directly to customers worldwide. Its products span wellness, electronics, household essentials, and digital solutions. Orbio employs more than 260 people and generated €400 million in revenue in 2025.

How do you build a business at that scale—and keep it growing profitably without external funding?

Join Vilnius Founders for an evening with Marius Buzaitis, Co-founder of Orbio World, exploring the journey behind those numbers: finding products people want, winning customers abroad, and building the teams that make it happen.

This interview will be in Lithuanian.

🗓️ OCT 15, 18.00 - 21.00
📍 Venue TBA!

Interested in joining Orbio?

Meet the team during networking after the interview and explore career opportunities: https://lnkd.in/d27x-raF

What we’ll discuss
- From idea to demand: how to test a product and decide whether to scale it or walk away.
- Winning customers abroad: what makes a product, brand, and marketing campaign work across different markets.
- Profitable growth: balancing advertising spend, customer retention, and margins.
- Building the team: which hires matter at each stage and how a founder’s role changes as the company grows.
- The difficult lessons: mistakes, failed experiments, and what Marius would do differently.

Expect an open fireside chat, audience questions, and networking over drinks. Come with a question, meet fellow founders and operators, and leave with ideas to apply to your own business.

Moderator: Edmundas Balčikonis, Founder of Vilnius Founders and CEO of Such Much AI.

About 🚀 Vilnius Founders https://lnkd.in/dHKcNgnh

Vilnius Founders brings together a community of 4,000+ founders, investors, and technology professionals through monthly meetups and online groups. We’ve hosted 30+ events, featuring founders of Vinted, TransferGo, Ovoko, Pulsetto, CoinGate, Ondato, and more.

No slides. No suits. Real examples, honest opinions, and meaningful connections.

🚀 Vilnius Founders are coming to London! 🇬🇧

Looking for customers, investors, or business partners in the UK? Join Vilnius Founders in London.

We’re partnering with the Lithuania - UK Business Forum 2026 and LCCUK - Lithuanian Chamber of Commerce in the UK to host events that connect founders with investors, business leaders, and potential customers in the UK.

Whether you’re exploring the market, already building there, or looking to connect with Lithuania’s startup community, we’d love to have you join us.
Register your interest to receive event details and information about pitching opportunities as they’re announced.

Agenda

You can participate in the Lithuania–UK Business Forum 2026 events you choose. Here are some of the activities exclusively designed for investors and startups from Lithuania:

1. OCT 21 - 1 PM to 3 PM: Reception at the Embassy of the Republic of Lithuania to the United Kingdom
- Lithuanian startup pitches
- Panel: Raising Your First Round: What UK Investors Look for in Lithuanian Startups
What makes an early-stage Lithuanian startup ready for UK investment—and what should founders prove before approaching investors?

2. Oct 21 - 6 PM to 8.30 PM: Evening networking event with UK investors and startups

3. Oct 22 - 9 AM to 5 PM: The main conference day at the Lithuania–UK Business Forum 2026
- Panel: Beyond Borders: Building Lithuania–UK Tech Partnerships
How Lithuanian and UK technology businesses turn connections into customers, commercial partnerships, and growth. Speakers will share real examples of finding partners, building trust, negotiating deals, and overcoming challenges—with lessons relevant to businesses across sectors.
- 5 PM to 9 PM - Closing Reception & Networking
- 6 PM to 8 PM - VIP Networking event for selected senior executives.

4. OCT 23 - 12 PM to 2.30 PM: Exclusive Business Networking Reception at the House of Lords

About Vilnius Founders

Vilnius Founders brings together 4,000+ founders, investors, and technology professionals. We organize monthly meetups and have hosted 30+ events, typically welcoming 200–500+ attendees in Vilnius.

Our past events have featured founders from Vinted, TransferGo, Ovoko, Pulsetto, CoinGate, Ondato, and other growing Lithuanian companies. Expect practical conversations about building businesses, finding customers, and raising funding — with plenty of time to meet fellow founders and investors.

RSVP: https://lnkd.in/dx9pEAJB

Fundraising & Winning in the US - home truths for European founders chasing those greenbacks

This week I was fortunate to be in the room in Vilnius when Edmundas Balčikonis of Vilnius Founders fireside-chatted Philip H. Beauregard of Impellent Ventures. Phil is a former successful serial entrepreneur turned angel investor and now VC. He sold his first company Rekindle to Hubspot.

Over the course of an hour, Phil laid out the truth about raising US VC investment to a large gathering of founders. He was extremely candid about (a) how difficult this is to do and (b) how badly prepared most European founders are in terms of entering the US market.

The key takeaway for me was that there are 2 paths to bag a US VC. The first is for your startup to reach what Phil calls “F*ck You Velocity” (FYV) in a short space of time. He thinks getting to $1m ARR from $0 in 3 months is about the right metric that will result in VCs paying attention along with being able to demonstrate that buyers love and want to carry on using your stuff. It’s ok if you spend 6 or 12 months before that with no revenue & also ok if meteoric takeoff happens after a pivot. I know from experience that this is possible but boy does it require a relentless focus on sales & storytelling. If you can do this you may decide you don’t need to raise … and you can keep all that lovely equity for the founding team. The second path is to meet and pitch to hundreds of potential investors hoping to find what Phil calls a “true believer” … but he adds that this is as difficult as finding a spouse.

I asked him later what percentage of European founders go with the first option & that rapid growth mindset. He didn’t give me an exact number but he did use the word minuscule.

There were many other golden nuggets but sadly not enough characters left to include them. I loved this though – “The best exits happen when companies are bought not sold - running a process will get a different ($) result from unsolicited inbound interest”.

And he used my favourite Steve Jobs quote - Why join the navy when you can be a pirate? Remember that one the next day you’re on the downward trajectory of the startup roller coaster.

Last & maybe an important point - Phil asks every founder who pitches to him “What’s the worst thing you’ve ever been through in your life?” He hopes they will answer but gives them the option to abstain.

The talk made me think about how we help our AwakenHub founders in terms of the US. As well as making warm introductions from our own extensive US networks we work hard with the companies we believe in to bring US-based angels from our AwakenAngels syndicate onto the cap table early doors. This approach has already paid dividends for some of our earlier portfolio companies who’ve gone on to raise additional investment in the US … maybe it’s a variation on the true believer strand.

Hope this read helps someone. Always worth considering if the juice is worth the squeeze.
